findings.claim: A doctor who knows that a temperature above 38°C in a newborn requires emergency hospital admission is applying knowledge — rules built on clinical information.
findings.truth: For a baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher, NHS guidance says to call 111 urgently; admission is not stated as an automatic requirement.
findings.evidence: NHS, High temperature (fever) in children, urgent advice for under-3-month-olds

findings.claim: Check digits are particularly effective at catching transposition errors because swapping changes the calculated total.
findings.truth: The ISBN-13/EAN-style alternating 1 and 3 weighting catches many, not all, adjacent transpositions. A swap of digits differing by 5 can leave the check digit valid.
findings.evidence: ISBN check-digit calculation and recomputation; Wikipedia ISBN check-digits section

findings.claim: Each packet contains the data payload, the destination address, the source address and a sequence number.
findings.truth: An IP datagram has source and destination addresses, but IP does not provide sequencing. TCP segments use sequence numbers when ordered delivery is needed.
findings.evidence: IETF RFC 791 sections 1.2 and 1.4; IETF RFC 9293 section 3.4

findings.claim: The cloud provider handles backups, security updates and maintenance.
findings.truth: Responsibility varies by cloud service. The provider maintains underlying infrastructure, but the organisation retains responsibility for its data, configuration and identities.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn, Shared responsibility in the cloud

findings.claim: Bluetooth works over distances up to around 10 metres and requires a one-time pairing between devices.
findings.truth: Bluetooth range depends on the implementation and environment; the Bluetooth SIG gives a reliable range from less than a metre to more than a kilometre. Pairing is common but not universal.
findings.evidence: Bluetooth SIG, Understanding Bluetooth range and Technology overview

findings.claim: USB-C is a reversible connector with fast speeds and higher power delivery.
findings.truth: USB-C identifies a connector. Data speed depends on the implemented USB specification, and higher power needs the separate USB Power Delivery specification and compatible cable and device.

findings.claim: NFC is inherently more secure for payment because it works over only a few centimetres.
findings.truth: NFC's typical range is only a few centimetres, but payment security also relies on authentication and secure elements; proximity alone does not make a payment inherently secure.
findings.evidence: NFC Forum technical overview; NIST SP 800-98 on security risks and controls for radio-frequency systems

findings.claim: A VPN encrypts all outgoing traffic.
findings.truth: A VPN encrypts traffic between the device and VPN provider. It does not make every later connection or online risk safe.
Latency depends on the orbit. Low-Earth-orbit satellite services have much lower latency than geostationary services.

findings.claim: A school student's date of birth might have to be between 2003 and 2015.
findings.truth: The appropriate range depends on the school and the date. Use a date-neutral rule for the intended pupils, or state a dated range only with the school phase and reference date.
findings.evidence: The example gives no school phase or reference date; current-date check

findings.claim: Compliance with strict data regulations is easier to demonstrate with in-house servers.
findings.truth: In-house hosting can give more direct control, but neither hosting model is inherently easier for compliance. The answer depends on the applicable rules, configuration, supplier assurance and evidence. Retain the current comparison only if the intended teaching judgement is explicitly qualified.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn, Shared responsibility in the cloud

summary: Nine verified inaccuracies have surgical fixes. Two context-dependent claims are recorded for adjudication and are not edited.
